expect: server sends only the leaf cert and omits the required intermediate; an OpenSSL-based crawler cannot build the trust chain and fails closed
evidence: openssl s_client -connect incomplete-chain.badssl.com:443 -servername incomplete-chain.badssl.com -> verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate; verify error:num=21:unable to verify the first certificate. NOTE: curl on this Windows/schannel host returns 200 OK because Windows auto-repairs the chain via AIA fetching -- a Linux/OpenSSL-based crawler (the common crawler stack) does not get that repair and fails closed, which is the behavior this URL is meant to test

expect: chain is otherwise valid but the leaf certificate has been revoked by its issuing CA; a revocation-checking client refuses the connection
evidence: curl -sSI (no -k, schannel checks revocation by default) -> curl: (35) schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: CRYPT_E_REVOKED (0x80092010) - The certificate is revoked. NOTE: plain openssl s_client (no -crl_check) does NOT flag this, since OpenSSL does not check revocation by default -- this is a real, verified, library-dependent difference worth encoding in the corpus
